??? quote "Dialogue"

    - There it is, *Player*. The first true map of the Sounding Caves. My name, and yours beside it. Grandfather would have laughed. The real laugh, this time.
    - I told you about the water. I've told nobody else. Let's finish it, you and me.
    - An A, by a tide mark. That far in, and he never said. Not once.
    - You found Ronan before I did. With my rope! I owe you. And he owes me a rope.
    - Gwenna's map! Well, a map, and a lecture. I've read the map three times. The lecture once. Mostly.
    - So? Caves, coves or a drink? Any order.
        - *Choice:* Who are you?
        - *Choice:* The sea caves?
        - *Choice:* Ronan?
        - *Choice:* Take me to the Sounding Caves.
        - *Choice:* Take me to the Still Pool.
        - *Choice:* Goodbye.
    - Lachlan, adventurer, coves-born. My grandfather Alasdair raised me. He'd been everywhere on this coast in a little boat and had a story for every rock.
    - I've his old oilskin and his tide-reckoner, and I use both. He went a little way into the sea caves once, as a young man, and came out faster than he went in. He laughed about it. I never quite believed the laugh.
    - The sea caves under the cliffs. The mouths open at low water and the sea booms in and out. Nobody's mapped them. I've marked every mouth from the Inlet Quay to the far cove, with the tide to go in by.
    - A few dozen yards in, most of them. A bit further in two. Every trip I go deeper. First I need Gwenna's old maps. She keeps saying no.
    - The Sounding Caves, I'm calling them, for the noise. The Mouths first, then down past Gwenna's Drop. Every trip a bit deeper. You're coming, of course.
    - You know about the moving water now. The only one who does. I'm not turning back again. Not with you there.
    - Mapped, end to end, Still Pool and all. Next I'll map something nobody has even heard of. Give me a week.
    - The little magpie from the coves. I let him carry my rope to the quay once and he's never let me forget it. He wants to come to the caves. "When you are bigger," I tell him. I've started to worry he won't wait.
    - I still tell him "when you are bigger". After that day I said it differently, and he heard it. I think he'll wait now. I hope he will.
    - Off you go. Mind the tide. It doesn't mind you.
    - Low water, the Fishers' Coves, the third mouth along. Follow me and mind your head.
    - Past the Long Echo. Listen. You can hear it breathing from here.
